liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **On The Road Again** (1 review): Rarely played, especially electrically, per the reviewer [19]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Described as very well done, within a first set of top-shelf Garcia playing [15]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Called phenomenal, with Weir's tasteful slide playing picked up and shredded by Garcia [15]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Lazy Lightning into Supplication pairing as a good stretch of the show [11]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Reviewer asks why Brent's keyboards cannot be heard on this song [21]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Reviewer notes any 1980s show containing Casey Jones is notable [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **Do Right Woman, Do Right Man (Joan Baez solo)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **Don't Blame My Mother (Joan Baez solo)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **The Boxer (Joan Baez solo)**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]
- **Happy New Year In Arabic (Joan Baez & Mickey Hart)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **Lady Di (Joan Baez & GD)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **Barbara Allen (Joan Baez & GD)**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-12-30.167453.nak300.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 27 songs; 171 min [1]
- **gd1981-12-30.147937.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: source not stated; 27 songs; 169 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1981-12-30.nak700.anon-severson-poris.LMPP.96582.flac16**: source not stated; 28 songs; 172 min [4]. Said about its sound: Tape pauses between some tracks, and the mix changes just after It's All Over Now begins; still called a great recording [4]
- **gd1981-12-30.sbd.munder.hempel.patched-8211.90866.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: The soundboard mix is good but slightly heavy on Brent's keyboards [15]
- **gd81-12-30.sbd.munder.8211.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [8]. Said about its sound: Brent's keyboards sit too high in the mix, with a tinkly tone that overshadows guitar, notably on They Love Each Other and Cumberland Blues [12]
- **gd1981-12-30.sbd.miller.117246.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 3.12/5 by 8 [9]. Said about its sound: Miller transfer has a canned sound, too much treble, too little Phil, and oddly distorted vocals at times [17]

## Around the show

- Attendee decided last minute to drive over, found walk-up tickets at the box office amid a chaotic crowd at the auditorium front [16]
- Found the show fairly nondescript and uninspired, having expected Joan Baez to be the night's highlight [16]
- Attendee was 17 years old at the show [18]
- Joan Baez sang Do Right Woman, Don't Blame My Mother and The Boxer solo; Brent did not play on Do Right Woman or the Arabic New Year song [1]
- Brent Mydland did not play on Do Right Woman, Do Right Man or Happy New Year in Arabic [3]
- Mickey Hart joined Joan Baez for the Arabic New Year song; the full band joined her afterward [4]
- Joan Baez plays on the first three second-disc tracks; Brent is absent from the first four second-disc tracks [5]
- Reviewer attended every show of this run and rates this night above New Year's Eve, which they consider slightly overrated [12]
- Treated as a warm-up for the following night's New Year's Eve show, which the reviewer ranks among favorite NYE shows [17]
- Only show with Cumberland Blues, Dire Wolf and On the Road Again together; Cumberland and Dire Wolf paired just five times after 1972 [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-12-30.167453.nak300.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII C90) [1]. Also: A Nakamichi 700 source patches a short gap in They Love Each Other; an AKG 414 source patches Drums [1]
- **gd1981-12-30.147937.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: taped by Rip Tompkins & Richie Stankiewicz; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Source: BeyerDynamic M88's > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XLII-S 90's, recording by Rip Tompkins, & with thanks to Richie Stankiewicz! [3]. Also: Beyer-mic recording with patches added from the Nakamichi 700 source ID 96582 for Do Right Woman and Drums into Space [3]
- **gd1981-12-30.nak700.anon-severson-poris.LMPP.96582.flac16**: taped by anonymous taper, Jamie Poris, Mark Severson; transferred by Brian Green and SIRMick; source: Nak 700's - 3 mic mix (L & R Cardoids 6 db EQ, center Omni. 35' from stage) > Mixer > Sony TC-D5 > MAC (Maxell MX 90's) [4]. Also: Taped from the free throw line on the floor using a mic mixer built by Jaime; Mark Severson's masters were lent [4]
- **gd1981-12-30.sbd.munder.hempel.patched-8211.90866.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Thomas Hempel; source: mixed (see notes) [5]. Also: Soundboard lineage runs through cassette, PCM, DAT and CD, Cool Edit Pro, SHN, and FLAC, matching shnid 8211 [5]
- **gd81-12-30.sbd.munder.8211.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboad [8]
- **gd1981-12-30.sbd.miller.117246.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat -> CDSet 2 Pre Drums: SBD -> Cassette Master -> PCM -> Dat -> CDSet 2 Post Drums: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel ->… [9]
